title: BenchPreS: A Benchmark for Context-Aware Personalized Preference Selectivity of Persistent-Memory LLMs
abstract: arXiv:2603.16557v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) increasingly store user preferences in persistent memory to support personalization across interactions. However, in third-party communication settings governed by social and institutional norms, some user preferences may be inappropriate to apply. We introduce BenchPreS, which evaluates whether memory-based user preferences are appropriately applied or suppressed across communication contexts. Using two complementary metrics, Misapplication Rate (MR) and Appropriate Application Rate (AAR), we find even frontier LLMs struggle to apply preferences in a context-sensitive manner. Models with stronger preference adherence exhibit higher rates of over-application, and neither reasoning capability nor prompt-based defenses fully resolve this issue. These results suggest current LLMs treat personalized preferences as globally enforceable rules rather than as context-dependent normative signals.

translated_title: BenchPreS：面向持久记忆大语言模型的上下文感知个性化偏好选择性的基准测试
translated_abstract: 大语言模型（LLM）越来越多地将用户偏好存储在持久记忆中，以支持跨交互的个性化服务。然而，在受社会和制度规范约束的第三方交流场景中，某些用户偏好可能并不适合被应用。我们提出了BenchPreS基准，用于评估基于记忆的用户偏好在不同交流情境中是被适当地应用还是被抑制。通过两个互补的指标——误用率和适当应用率，我们发现即使是前沿的大语言模型也难以以情境敏感的方式应用偏好。偏好依从性更强的模型表现出更高的过度应用率，且无论是推理能力还是基于提示词的防御机制都无法完全解决这一问题。这些结果表明，当前的大语言模型将个性化偏好视为全局可执行的规则，而非依赖情境的规范性信号。
tldr: 该论文提出BenchPreS基准，用于评估具有持久记忆的大语言模型能否在不同交流情境下恰当地应用或抑制用户偏好，发现即使是前沿模型也倾向于将用户偏好当作全局规则而非情境依赖的信号来执行，且偏好依从性越强过度应用率越高。
